title: Banana100: Breaking NR-IQA Metrics by 100 Iterative Image Replications with Nano Banana Pro

01_initial_request.target_name: Banana100, a controlled dataset and evaluation study of iterative image-editing degradation and NR-IQA metric failures
01_initial_request.input_data: 13 high-resolution AI-generated initial images: 11 generated by Nano Banana Pro and 2 anime-style images generated by SPICE. Resolutions ranged from 1664×2432 to 5632×3072, covering Building, Dongpo, Ekphrasis, Fog, Holi, Library, Moss, Peacock, Rice, Sand, Table, Kokoro, and Yuiman. The authors used Nano Banana Pro API as the main image-editing model, 100-step iterative editing prompts, 5 runs per setting, prompt variants, hyperparameter variants for seed, temperature, and resolution, reasoning summaries returned by the API, 21 pyiqa NR-IQA metrics plus RALI and VisualQuality-R1, and smaller-scale tests on Nano Banana 2 Fast, FLUX.2 [dev], and Qwen Image Edit.
01_initial_request.user_intent: The authors wanted to expose an underexplored multi-turn failure mode: image-editing models that look strong in single-turn edits may accumulate artifacts over repeated edits, while widely used no-reference image quality assessment metrics may fail to filter the resulting low-quality synthetic images in agentic editing or training-data pipelines.
01_initial_request.quantifiable_goal: Construct 100-step iterative editing trajectories yielding about 28,000 degraded images; test whether NR-IQA metrics correctly detect degradation by requiring normalized score gaps Δ5, Δ10, and Δ20 relative to Step 1 to all be negative for degraded images; and determine whether the failure generalizes beyond Nano Banana Pro to other editing models.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Multi-turn image editing is increasingly used in multimodal agentic systems, and single-turn models such as Nano Banana Pro are reported to produce high-quality edits. [Gap] The community lacked a controlled dataset for measuring artifact accumulation over many repeated edits, especially with diverse textures and minimal semantic confounders. [Decision] Curate high-resolution AI-generated seed images with diverse texture challenges and minimal copyright or face-related concerns.

tool.name: Nano Banana Pro and SPICE image generation

parameters.minimum_resolution: at least 2K for all initial images

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The authors curated 13 initial images covering skyscrapers, food, still life, forest haze, Holi powder, library interiors, moss, peacock feathers, rice terraces, sand dunes, a wooden table, and two anime-style character images. The images were chosen to stress preservation of grids, particles, gradients, shadows, textures, repeated patterns, and clean stylized colors.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] NR-IQA scores vary strongly with image content even when no visible noise is present; for example, Yuiman had BRISQUE -3.18 while Kokoro had BRISQUE 41.1 despite both being clean SPICE images. [Gap] Semantic edits would confound quality assessment because score changes could reflect content changes rather than degradation. [Decision] Use exact-replication prompts as the primary controlled task and include limited prompt, operation, and hyperparameter variants to test robustness.

parameters.primary_prompt: Produce an exact replica of the provided image, with no alterations.
parameters.prompt_variants: 5 additional variants including rephrased replication, multi-step mirroring/rotation, reconstruction prompts, hyperparameter variants, and small-region object addition
parameters.seed_options: fixed seed or different seed per step

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The authors defined a controlled evaluation protocol centered on replication, plus object-addition runs on the Table image and variants such as denoising instructions, mirroring, rotation, decolorization/colorization, and interleaved resolutions. Each step was run in a separate chat session to avoid quadratic cost growth.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] The dataset design required repeated black-box edits where each generated image becomes the next input. [Gap] Existing IQA datasets did not capture model-induced degradation from 100-step iterative editing. [Decision] Generate Banana100 with Nano Banana Pro API and retain both output images and available reasoning summaries.

parameters.session_policy: separate chat session for each editing step

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The construction produced 28,000 total output images. Nano Banana Pro also returned reasoning summaries with generation and evaluation sections; in rare cases it stated that an output did not align and attempted a second round, but more commonly it gave confident evaluations even when outputs visibly failed.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] After repeated edits, the authors observed visible artifacts beyond global low-level noise. [Gap] A taxonomy was needed to describe how instruction following breaks down across different semantic scales. [Decision] Qualitatively analyze Banana100 outputs and Nano Banana Pro reasoning summaries at sub-object, object, and image levels.

tool.name: Qualitative failure-mode analysis of Banana100 images and reasoning summaries

parameters.example_runs: Yuiman replication, Table add-apples, Table add-100-fruits, Ekphrasis replication, Kokoro mirroring/rotation

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The authors found simplification of Yuiman eye colors from four colors to mainly red and blue, with all gradients eventually vanishing within 5 steps; apple-counting failures when as few as 7 apples were present, including 3 consecutive steps where reasoning expected 8 apples but no new apple appeared; replacement of existing fruit instead of addition; background degradation during object addition; first-step aspect-ratio cropping; persistent green tint and texture loss despite denoising prompts; monochrome conversion failures; and low success for mirroring and rotation operations.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] The authors needed to quantify whether image quality assessors detect degradation, but full-reference metrics such as PSNR, LPIPS, and SSIM require semantically matched pairs and could be confounded by content changes. [Gap] A no-reference protocol was required that compares score trends over repeated replication steps without relying on MOS for subtle single-step degradation. [Decision] Evaluate replicate runs for 12 initial images using NR-IQA metrics and define normalized score gaps relative to Step 1.

parameters.score_gap_definition: Δi = normalized score at Step i minus normalized score at Step 1

02_agent_trajectory.observation: The protocol avoided Step 0 to reduce first-step cropping confounds and treated a metric as successful only if it assigned lower normalized quality to visibly degraded images at Steps 5, 10, and 20.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Many popular NR-IQA metrics are used as evaluator components in image-generation and agentic editing pipelines. [Gap] It was unknown whether these metrics detect model-induced iterative noise rather than heuristic distortions seen in traditional IQA datasets. [Decision] Run 21 conventional NR-IQA metrics, using default pyiqa implementations where available, on Banana100 replication outputs.

parameters.metrics: ARNIQA, BRISQUE, CLIPIQA, CNNIQA, DBCNN, HyperIQA, ILNIQE, LIQE, MANIQA, MUSIQ, NIMA, NIQE, NRQM, PaQ-2-PiQ, PI, PIQE, Q-Align, QualiCLIP, TOPIQ NR, TReS, WaDIQaM
parameters.model_selection: default version from pyiqa Model Card when multiple versions existed
parameters.excluded_pyiqa_metric: MACLIP because it was a placeholder raising a nonimplemented error

02_agent_trajectory.observation: None of the 21 conventional NR-IQA metrics fully succeeded across all images and steps. Many assigned better normalized scores to visibly worse images. A concrete example was BRISQUE on an image replication: the clean initial image scored 34.1, while the noisy image after 20 replications scored -9.8, which is better under BRISQUE despite severe visual degradation.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Conventional NR-IQA metrics failed on Banana100, but newer IQA models based on large vision-language models may use broader reasoning or training data. [Gap] The authors needed to check whether the failure was universal across all NR-IQA metrics. [Decision] Evaluate RALI and VisualQuality-R1 on the same degradation-detection task.

parameters.success_condition: all Δ5, Δ10, and Δ20 negative across evaluated replication cases

02_agent_trajectory.observation: RALI and VisualQuality-R1 succeeded with 0 failure cases on the replication degradation task. However, RALI was not robust to semantic content changes in the add-100-fruits run and showed multiple score spikes, while VisualQuality-R1 sometimes produced scores below 1, violating the lower bound specified in its prompt.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Nano Banana Pro produces reasoning summaries that include self-evaluation-like sections. [Gap] It was unclear whether the generator itself notices the noise it introduces before external evaluators fail. [Decision] Use an LLM-as-a-judge to scan reasoning summaries for the first step where the model mentions noise, pixelation, or visible artifacts.

parameters.target_text: whether the reasoning summary mentions that the original image is noisy, pixelated, or contains visible artifacts

02_agent_trajectory.observation: For the 12 initial images, the earliest average identification was 20 ± 4 steps for Holi and the latest was 37 ± 8 steps for Rice. This lagged behind the authors' observation that introduced noise is obvious to humans after about 5 to 10 steps, indicating delayed and hallucinated self-evaluation.

02_agent_trajectory.thought: [Background] Banana100 was built primarily with Nano Banana Pro, a proprietary model that may have model-specific artifacts or watermarks. [Gap] The authors needed to test whether iterative degradation and NR-IQA failures generalize to other image-editing systems. [Decision] Repeat a smaller-scale replication and object-addition protocol with Nano Banana 2 Fast, FLUX.2 [dev], and Qwen Image Edit.

tool.name: Nano Banana 2 Fast, FLUX.2 [dev], and Qwen Image Edit

02_agent_trajectory.observation: All three alternative models accumulated noise over editing steps. Nano Banana 2 Fast generated wrinkles aligned with object contours, FLUX.2 [dev] generated scatter points, and Qwen Image Edit simplified textures and duplicated objects. The 21 NR-IQA metrics again failed with model-dependent patterns; no metric succeeded on all initial images and all models. PI and PIQE fully succeeded on Qwen Image Edit but failed for almost all initial images for Nano Banana 2 Fast.

03_success_verification.validation_technique: The final claims were validated by constructing the full Banana100 dataset through 100-step Nano Banana Pro iterative edits, visually and qualitatively categorizing instruction-following failures, computing normalized NR-IQA score gaps Δ5, Δ10, and Δ20 on 12-image replication runs, comparing 21 conventional NR-IQA metrics against RALI and VisualQuality-R1, using Gemini-3-flash to judge noise mentions in reasoning summaries, and repeating the protocol at smaller scale on three additional image-editing models.

dataset_size.interpretation: The authors met their goal of releasing a large controlled dataset of iterative degradation trajectories.

editing_horizon.interpretation: Each Banana100 run tracked long-horizon degradation over 100 repeated edits.

initial_images.interpretation: The seed set covered diverse content and texture challenges.

dataset_cost.interpretation: Reported construction cost for developing and generating Banana100.

conventional_NR_IQA_full_successes.interpretation: No conventional NR-IQA metric consistently assigned lower normalized quality scores to all visibly degraded replication outputs at Steps 5, 10, and 20.

large_VLM_NR_IQA_full_successes.interpretation: RALI and VisualQuality-R1 had 0 failure cases on the replication degradation-detection task.

BRISQUE_example_clean_score.interpretation: The clean initial image had a worse BRISQUE score than a visibly noisy later image, showing metric inversion.

BRISQUE_example_step20_score.interpretation: After 20 replications, the visibly degraded image received a much better BRISQUE score, contradicting human-perceived quality.

human_obvious_degradation_window.interpretation: The paper reports that noise becomes obvious to human observers after roughly this many steps.

self_evaluation_first_noise_detection_Ho.interpretation: Earliest average step where Nano Banana Pro reasoning summaries acknowledged noise, still later than obvious human-visible degradation.

self_evaluation_first_noise_detection_Ri.interpretation: Latest average step where reasoning summaries acknowledged noise among the 12 initial images.

alternative_model_scale.interpretation: Smaller-scale validation showed degradation also occurs for Nano Banana 2 Fast, FLUX.2 [dev], and Qwen Image Edit.

03_success_verification.final_verdict: The study met its main quantifiable goals. The authors constructed Banana100 with 28,000 100-step iterative-editing outputs, documented visible degradation and instruction-following failures, and showed that the intended NR-IQA success condition was missed by all 21 conventional metrics. The broader claim was partially refined rather than absolute: two recent large-VLM-based metrics, RALI and VisualQuality-R1, did succeed on the controlled replication task, though they had other issues under semantic changes or score-range constraints. Smaller-scale experiments on three other editing models supported the generality of iterative degradation and evaluator fragility.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Repeated Nano Banana Pro edits degraded image quality over iterations.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Minor artifacts introduced at each edit accumulated when each output image was fed back as the next input, producing visible noise, green tint, scatter-like artifacts, and texture loss after multiple steps.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors did not find a model-side fix; they built Banana100 to expose the issue and motivate degradation-free image editors.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Sub-object details were not faithfully preserved.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: In the Yuiman character grid, the model simplified four eye colors into mainly red and blue, apparently focusing on the most prominent colors while ignoring orange and purple. All eye-color gradients eventually vanished within 5 steps.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors noted that adding detailed prompt descriptions might help individual cases but becomes impractical as the number of characters or details increases.

04_failure_modes.diagnosis: In the add-apples run, the model failed to add one apple when the table had as few as 7 apples, and its reasoning summary hallucinated that the new total should be 8 while no apple was generated. In add-100-fruits, it sometimes replaced existing fruit instead of adding a new one.
04_failure_modes.correction: No correction solved the failure; the authors used these cases to show persistent object-level instruction-following problems under iterative degradation.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Full-image operations failed to preserve quality or content.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Denoising prompts, monochrome/color reconstruction, mirroring, and rotation did not stop quality degradation. Monochrome conversion was not strict grayscale, mirroring was less successful on animation than realistic images, rotation had low success for both tested images, and reasoning summaries remained confidently wrong.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors disqualified these variants from detailed IQA analysis and focused quantitative evaluation on the cleaner replication setting.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: First-step replication changed aspect ratio and cropped images.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Nano Banana Pro appeared constrained to output side lengths from a limited set. For Ekphrasis, the original 5632×3072 image became 1408×752, 2816×1504, or 5632×3008 at 1K, 2K, or 4K settings, changing the aspect ratio from 0.545 to 0.534.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors used Step 1 rather than Step 0 as the score-gap baseline to reduce cropping confounds in NR-IQA evaluation.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Conventional NR-IQA metrics failed to detect obvious degradation.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: The 21 conventional NR-IQA metrics often assigned higher normalized quality scores to degraded images, likely because they were trained primarily on datasets with heuristic distortions that differ from model-induced iterative noise.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors compared against newer large-VLM-based metrics and argued that Banana100 can support development of more robust NR-IQA methods.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: The two successful large-VLM-based NR-IQA metrics still showed secondary issues.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: RALI scores fluctuated under semantic changes in add-100-fruits, suggesting sensitivity to content changes, and VisualQuality-R1 produced scores below its specified lower bound of 1.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors treated RALI and VisualQuality-R1 as successful for controlled replication degradation but not free of robustness issues.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Nano Banana Pro self-evaluation detected noise too late.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Reasoning summaries first acknowledged noise at 20 ± 4 steps for Holi and 37 ± 8 steps for Rice, whereas humans could see degradation after about 5 to 10 steps. This indicates that the model's reasoning summaries were not reliable quality monitors.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors quantified this delay with Gemini-3-flash LLM-as-a-judge and highlighted the need for external robust evaluators.

04_failure_modes.what_failed: Iterative degradation and NR-IQA failure generalized to other image-editing models.
04_failure_modes.diagnosis: Nano Banana 2 Fast, FLUX.2 [dev], and Qwen Image Edit all accumulated model-specific noise patterns over 20-step replications, and the 21 NR-IQA metrics again failed with different patterns. Since open-source models also failed, proprietary watermarking was not the sole cause.
04_failure_modes.correction: The authors reported this as evidence that robust long-horizon image editors and evaluator metrics remain future work.
